answer:
For adults with type 2 diabetes, the American Diabetes Association (ADA) recommends annual dilated eye exams to screen for diabetic retinopathy. Additionally, an annual comprehensive foot exam with monofilament testing should be conducted to check for peripheral neuropathy, starting from diagnosis. These screenings are part of their guidelines on microvascular complications in diabetes [ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes 2024].

There is also a recommendation regarding glycemic targets and pharmacologic approaches. For non-pregnant adults with type 2 diabetes who do not experience significant hypoglycemia, an A1C goal of less than 7% is proposed, with metformin as the initial pharmacological agent [ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes 2024].

While these recommendations cover aspects of management and screening for diabetes, it's important to consult your healthcare provider for a comprehensive yearly check-up including any additional recommended screenings or treatments that may be specific to their condition.
